title: Metallic conductors and filament-lamp I–V characteristics
prior_knowledge_summary: AS Topic 1 quantities and units, including SI base units, derived units and unit conversions.
learning_goals: Sketch and interpret the I–V characteristic of a metallic conductor at constant temperature.
Explain the changing resistance of a filament lamp as its current and temperature rise.
new_learning: Linear ohmic and curved filament-lamp I–V characteristics, including gradient and temperature reasoning.
not_yet_taught: sketch the I–V characteristics of a metallic conductor at constant temperature, a semiconductor diode and a filament lamp
recall and use R = ρL / A
understand that the resistance of a light-dependent resistor (LDR) decreases as the light intensity increases
understand that the resistance of a thermistor decreases as the temperature increases (it will be assumed that thermistors have a negative temperature coefficient)
knowledge_boundary: Includes metallic conductors and filament lamps. The semiconductor diode characteristic is taught next; circuit-network applications remain deferred.

can_assume: sketch the I–V characteristics of a metallic conductor at constant temperature, a semiconductor diode and a filament lamp
explain that the resistance of a filament lamp increases as current increases because its temperature increases

past_paper_evidence.whole_question_context_policy: Resolve through the topic P2 index and retain complete question context.
